subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should OpenClaw allow configured model fallback after context-overflow recovery is exhausted, and what replay-safety and context-window constraints must gate it?
rationale: Both outcomes are defensible: current code and docs keep overflow inside compaction/retry, while the report identifies a real long-session recovery gap that crosses provider routing, replay safety, and session semantics.

options.title: Implement Guarded Larger-Window Fallback
options.body: Allow fallback only after compaction and truncation fail, only to candidates with known sufficient effective context, while preserving replay-safety and delivery guards.

options.title: Keep Compaction-Only Behavior
options.body: Document that context overflow is not a model-fallback trigger and improve user-facing recovery guidance instead.

options.title: Defer To Narrower UX Work
options.body: Prioritize diagnostics and model-switch recovery items while leaving larger-context fallback as a future policy decision.

recommendation.title: Implement Guarded Larger-Window Fallback
recommendation.body: Allow fallback only after compaction and truncation fail, only to candidates with known sufficient effective context, while preserving replay-safety and delivery guards.
